Kyle / Sana — thanks for the sync earlier today. Quick recap of the performance items we committed to validate for the Private (VPC) deployment and the concrete next steps so we can schedule the connectivity window. I summarized what we heard on the call and added Redwood's target ranges that we'll use as acceptance guidance. Please correct anything I mis-stated.

Summary of requirements and Redwood targets (provisional):
- End-to-end p95 latency (app -> model host -> back to app) for non-streaming requests: <= 250 ms for responses up to 256 tokens.
- Streaming per-token transmit latency (first-byte-to-client for a single token): p95 <= 60 ms, tail under 120 ms.
- Sustained throughput: baseline 1,000 tokens/sec; burst capacity up to 5,000 tokens/sec for short bursts (30–60s).
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent long-lived streaming sessions with predictable per-connection latency.
- Connection reliability: TCP retransmit tolerance up to +40 ms extra RTT before noticeable decoding stalls.
- Egress bandwidth: recommend 1 Gbps headroom for peak bursts; we’ll aim to validate with parallel token streams during the test.

Network-path specifics we discussed (items to confirm):
- Preferred: direct cloud peering between Finexa colo and Redwood edge (target network RTT < 10 ms).
- Fallback: IPSec VPN over your existing MPLS backbone (expect additional 20–60 ms overhead depending on encryption and path).
- MTU/Jumbo frame support — helps reduce CPU overhead for high-throughput token streams.
- BGP/ASN info to enable peering (if peering selected).

Action items / next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Finexa: share traceroute + pcap from client app -> target Redwood egress IPs (Kyle) — target: today or tomorrow. Attachment stub accepted.
2) Redwood: share SLO matrix + connectivity checklist (attached redwood-slo-matrix-v1.xlsx). (Evelyn) — done.
3) Finexa & Redwood: decide peering vs VPN and confirm IPs, ASN, and ports to whitelist. (Kyle / Sana) — target: 48 hours.
4) Schedule a 60–90 minute connectivity/throughput window (end-to-end perf tests + streaming demo). (All) — propose Wed 2027-07-28 09:00 PT as a starting option.
5) Finexa: provide expected typical message size and median token length for sample traces (Sana).

Attachments: redwood-slo-matrix-v1.xlsx, connectivity-checklist-v2.pdf (stubs attached).

Thanks — I’ll hold the slot tentatively for Wed 7/28. If peering is doable earlier we can compress the schedule.

Thanks — good notes. A few technical clarifications and pre-test requests from the Redwood infra side so our runbook is ready: 

1) IP + port whitelist: we’ll provide two egress IPs and a TCP port range for the public-facing test endpoints. Please confirm whether you prefer our standard ports (443 and 5200–5210) or a custom ephemeral set.

2) Packet capture: the pcap is useful — can you also include a short sample of the application-level payload (redacted is fine) to confirm framing and token sizes? We need to simulate realistic request/response sizes during the streaming run.

3) MTU and jumbo frames: please confirm MTU across the path. If we can enable 9000 MTU inside the peering/vlan, it reduces CPU pressure during token bursts.

4) Encryption overhead: if VPN uses AES-GCM with hardware offload, overhead tends to be modest (~5–15 ms). If VPN goes through a CPU-bound appliance in the colo, we may see larger overheads — call this out.

5) Test plan: we’ll run two phases during the window — (A) connectivity + latency baseline (short pings, 10 parallel connections) and (B) streaming throughput ramp (50 -> 200 concurrent streams over 10 minutes). We’ll record p50/p95/p99 for token transmit times.

Actionable for Finexa before the test: share expected peak concurrent sessions and a sample payload (even synthetic) so we can provision accurate token generation in the load runner.

I’ll prepare the port/IP ranges and a short test harness script. If you’re okay, Jordan will operate the run from our side during the window.

—
